We’re ready to sign a temporary agreement and reimburse for extra capacity. Please advise what you need from us (model pinning, certs, IP allowlist, contact for 24/7 escalation).

Thanks for the ping, Karthik — see quick product-level callouts. I skimmed the forecast and the primary risk is quality regressions if we move to any quantized model variant without pre-run evals on their prompt set. My recommendations: 

1) Model pinning: require Alpha to pin to the validated model snapshot we use in production (redwood-v2-medium). We can offer redwood-v2-small as a fallback but only for non-critical requests.
2) Streaming: ask Alpha if they can tolerate non-streaming responses for the burst window (batching non-streamed requests saves tokens/instances and increases throughput headroom). If they accept, ops can autoscale more aggressively.
3) Rate shaping: implement burst windows with a soft-fail policy — allow 12k rps for 10 minutes every hour, then drop to 2k rps with standard throttles. This reduces sustained tail risk.
4) Evals: we need their top 50 prompt examples to run a quick smoke test against the fallback variant. Can Alpha provide by EOD tomorrow?

If ops can guarantee the ingress pattern for the time window and Sales signs off on credits, product is ok with a temporary SLA exemption provided the customer agrees to the model-pin + test-prompt requirements.

Quick ops update — we can support the requested window with these constraints and actions: 

- Capacity: We can provision an autoscale policy to cover the 12k rps 10–15m bursts for the 48-hour window if we temporarily lift the per-minute quota to 400k for Alpha. That requires a one-time engineering on-call during the window and a capacity reservation ticket.
- Fallback: In the event of persistent overload, we will implement routing to redwood-v2-small with token limits and an immediate customer-facing throttle at 3k rps to preserve platform stability.
- Lead time & ops tasks: need sign-off by EOD 05/25 to spin up the reservation, plus a signed SLA_exemption_request_AlphaApps.pdf and a PO or credit card auth for overage billing.
- Monitoring: Set up a dedicated Grafana dashboard and alert channel (#inc-alphaapps-launch) — ops will monitor and trigger fallback if error rate > 1.5% for 5m.

I’ll open the capacity reservation ticket after we have the sign-off and billing confirmation. If Sales approves a credit for the extra capacity, we can treat the expense as a promo credit against Q2 ARR.

4) Monitoring & rollback: we will create a dedicated dashboard and alerting channel; ops will trigger fallback routing if error rate exceeds thresholds.
